comment:
* The class that controls the behavior of the {@link SortedList}. *

* It defines how items should be sorted and how duplicates should be handled. *

* SortedList calls the callback methods on this class to notify changes about the underlying * data.

methods.name: public abstract int compare(T2 o1, T2 o2)
methods.comment:
* Similar to {@link java.util.Comparator#compare(Object, Object)}, should compare two and
         * return how they should be ordered.
         *
         * @param o1 The first object to compare.
         * @param o2 The second object to compare.
         *
         * @return a negative integer, zero, or a positive integer as the
         * first argument is less than, equal to, or greater than the
         * second.

methods.name: public abstract void onInserted(int position, int count)
methods.comment:
* Called by the SortedList when an item is inserted at the given position.
         *
         * @param position The position of the new item.
         * @param count    The number of items that have been added.

methods.name: public abstract void onRemoved(int position, int count)
methods.comment:
* Called by the SortedList when an item is removed from the given position.
         *
         * @param position The position of the item which has been removed.
         * @param count    The number of items which have been removed.

methods.name: public abstract void onMoved(int fromPosition, int toPosition)
methods.comment:
* Called by the SortedList when an item changes its position in the list.
         *
         * @param fromPosition The previous position of the item before the move.
         * @param toPosition   The new position of the item.

methods.name: public abstract void onChanged(int position, int count)
methods.comment:
* Called by the SortedList when the item at the given position is updated.
         *
         * @param position The position of the item which has been updated.
         * @param count    The number of items which has changed.

methods.name: public abstract boolean areContentsTheSame(T2 oldItem, T2 newItem)
methods.comment:
* Called by the SortedList when it wants to check whether two items have the same data * or not. SortedList uses this information to decide whether it should call * {@link #onChanged(int, int)} or not. *

* SortedList uses this method to check equality instead of {@link Object#equals(Object)} * so * that you can change its behavior depending on your UI. *

* For example, if you are using SortedList with a {@link android.support.v7.widget.RecyclerView.Adapter * RecyclerView.Adapter}, you should * return whether the items' visual representations are the same or not. * * @param oldItem The previous representation of the object. * @param newItem The new object that replaces the previous one. * * @return True if the contents of the items are the same or false if they are different.

methods.name: public abstract boolean areItemsTheSame(T2 item1, T2 item2)
methods.comment:
* Called by the SortedList to decide whether two object represent the same Item or not. *

* For example, if your items have unique ids, this method should check their equality. * * @param item1 The first item to check. * @param item2 The second item to check. * * @return True if the two items represent the same object or false if they are different.

methodNames: public abstract int compare(T2 o1, T2 o2)
public abstract void onInserted(int position, int count)
public abstract void onRemoved(int position, int count)
public abstract void onMoved(int fromPosition, int toPosition)
public abstract void onChanged(int position, int count)
public abstract boolean areContentsTheSame(T2 oldItem, T2 newItem)
public abstract boolean areItemsTheSame(T2 item1, T2 item2)
